findings.evidence: Deliver, Receive and Follow up occupy 39 of the 101 H2-section lines and contain substantial standard coaching guidance and repeated examples: "Reply to instances; turn labels into a request for an instance", "Do not argue the label; ask for one recent example and what it affected", and the subsequent sample repeat the same familiar technique. The strongest knowledge delta is concentrated in the routing rules, exceptions and gotchas rather than throughout the body.
findings.fix: Compress familiar SBI mechanics and the repeated label-to-example guidance into brief activation reminders. Retain the thin-versus-missing-evidence branch, disputed-evidence handling, power-specific rules, actionable recap fields, check-in defaults and silent omission of private details.

findings.evidence: The pre-send gate applies to "every draft" and requires it to be "written for private delivery"; line 100 reinforces private delivery even when a channel post is requested. This appropriately constrains corrective feedback but unnecessarily applies the same restriction to specific-work recognition and non-personal shared-work updates.
findings.fix: Scope mandatory private delivery to individual corrective feedback and sensitive content. Permit requested, recipient-approved public recognition and non-personal norm or ownership updates in appropriate shared channels when the confidentiality test passes; preserve the existing live-versus-written guidance for corrective feedback.

findings.evidence: The routing table sends "One incident, or recognition" to "SBI opener plus one open question", while line 49 says recognition names the behavior and effect, "then stops". Following the table literally adds a question to a recognition message that the dedicated recognition instruction says should end.
findings.fix: Give recognition its own routing-table row: name the specific behavior and its verified effect, then stop. Reserve the SBI opener plus open question route for corrective feedback.
